questions.question: A coordinate grid has an x-axis and a y-axis that cross at the origin, and each square stands for 1 unit in both directions. Priya builds a table of values for the relation y = 3x using x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, then plots one dot for each pair. Which dot lands in Quadrant III?
options: (-2, -6), because it is 2 left and 6 down
(2, -6), because it is 2 right and 6 down
(-2, 6), because it is 2 left and 6 up
(2, 6), because it is 2 right and 6 up
questions.explain: For x = -2, y = 3(-2) = -6, so the dot goes 2 left and 6 down, which is Quadrant III. The usual slip is keeping x positive and landing in Quadrant IV instead.

questions.question: On a coordinate grid where each square is 1 unit and both axes run from -10 to 10, Elijah makes a table of values for y = 2x + 1 using the five integer inputs x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2. He plots all five dots in the correct places. What should he do next to finish the graph?
options: Draw a straight line through the five dots and add arrows
Leave the five dots separate, since only 5 x-values fit
Join the dots with short segments, one dot to the next dot
Draw a dashed line through the dots to show the pattern
questions.explain: The table gives only those five integer inputs, so nothing exists between the dots. Any line, solid or dashed, would wrongly claim that inputs like x = 0.5 are part of the relation.

questions.question: A coordinate grid has the origin in the middle, and on this grid each square stands for 5 units on both axes. Nadia makes a table of values for y = x + 5 using x = -10, -5, 0, 5, 10, so the y-values are -5, 0, 5, 10, 15. Where does she put the dot for x = -10?
options: 1 square left of the origin, then 2 squares down
2 squares right of the origin, then 1 square down
2 squares left of the origin, then 1 square down
2 squares left of the origin, then 1 square up
questions.explain: The pair is (-10, -5) and each square is 5 units, so the dot is 2 squares left and 1 square down, in Quadrant III. The common trap is dropping the negative on x and counting squares to the right.

questions.question: A coordinate grid has axes running from -8 to 8, and each square stands for 1 unit. Owen makes a table of values for the relation y = 2x using x = -3, -1, 1, 3. Which list shows the four dots he should plot?
questions.explain: Double each x and keep its sign: -3 gives -6 and 3 gives 6, so two dots sit down-left in Quadrant III and two sit up-right in Quadrant I. Flipping the sign of y, or writing the pair backwards, sends the dots into the wrong quadrants.

questions.question: The relation y = -2x + 1 is graphed as separate dots for the integer values of x from -3 to 3. Which of these dots lies in Quadrant II?
options: the point for x = -3, which is (-3, 7)
the point for x = -3, which is (-3, -7)
the point for x = 3, which is (3, -5)
the point for x = 3, which is (3, 7)
questions.explain: Substitute carefully: -2(-3) + 1 = 6 + 1 = 7, so the dot is at (-3, 7), which is left of the y-axis and above the x-axis, in Quadrant II. Watch the double negative, since -2 times -3 is +6, not -6.

questions.question: Devon tracks his bank balance with y = 15x - 45, where y is dollars and x is the number of whole weeks from today (x = -3 to 3, and a negative x means weeks ago). He plots all 7 points in the right places, then rules a solid line through them. What one change makes his graph correct?
options: Keep the line and add arrows on both of its ends
Erase the line and leave the 7 points on their own
Keep the line but draw it dashed instead of solid
Keep the line but stop it at the first and last point
questions.explain: The balance is only counted in whole weeks, so the 7 points must stay separate. A line, even a dashed one, would claim there is a balance at 2.5 weeks, which the table never gives.

questions.question: A table of values for y = 5x + 5 uses x = -3, -2, -1, 0, 1. The five pairs are plotted on axes where each square stands for 5 units. Which statement describes where the five dots land?
options: Two are in Quadrant II, two in Quadrant IV, one on an axis
Three are in Quadrant III, one in Quadrant I, one on an axis
Two are in Quadrant III, one in Quadrant I, two on the axes
Two are in Quadrant II, one in Quadrant IV, two on the axes
questions.explain: The pairs are (-3, -10), (-2, -5), (-1, 0), (0, 5) and (1, 10): the first two are down-left in Quadrant III and (1, 10) is up-right in Quadrant I, while (-1, 0) and (0, 5) sit on the axes and belong to no quadrant.

questions.question: A discrete linear relation has been graphed as five dots at (-6, -4), (-3, -2), (0, 0), (3, 2) and (6, 4). Which statement about this graph is true?
options: Two dots lie in Quadrant II and two lie in Quadrant IV
The dots should be joined, since the pattern keeps going
Three dots lie in Quadrant III and two lie in Quadrant I
Two dots lie in Quadrant III and two lie in Quadrant I
questions.explain: Negative x with negative y is down-left, which is Quadrant III, and positive with positive is up-right, which is Quadrant I. The dot (0, 0) is the origin, so it sits on the axes and counts in no quadrant.

questions.question: A parkade at a Victoria mall numbers its floors with x: the floors x = -3, -2, -1 are underground and x = 1, 2 are above ground. The height of floor x above the ground, in metres, is y = 3x. Karim graphs a dot for every floor. Which statement is true for the floor x = -3?
options: It is plotted at (-3, -9) in Quadrant III, and the dots stay separate
It is plotted at (-3, 9) in Quadrant II, and the dots stay separate
It is plotted at (3, -9) in Quadrant IV, and the dots stay separate
It is plotted at (-3, -9) in Quadrant III, and the dots are joined up
questions.explain: Floor -3 gives y = 3(-3) = -9, so the dot is 3 left and 9 down, in Quadrant III. Because there is no floor -2.5, the dots are never joined.

questions.question: A creek near Chilliwack is measured once a day. Its depth compared with the marker is y = 5x - 15 centimetres, where x is the number of days from today and x takes the integer values from -2 to 4 (a negative x means days ago). All 7 points are graphed on four-quadrant axes. Which statement is correct?
options: 6 dots are below the x-axis, and the dots are not joined
5 dots are below the x-axis, and the dots are not joined
5 dots are below the x-axis, so join them to show the rise
7 dots are below the x-axis, and a solid line is drawn in
questions.explain: Only x = -2 to 2 give negative depths (-25, -20, -15, -10, -5), so 5 dots sit below the axis; x = 3 gives 0, which is on the axis, not below it. Since the creek is read once a day, the dots must stay separate.

questions.question: Ravi graphs y = -3x for x = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 on grid paper. He plots all five points in the correct spots, then rules a solid line through them with an arrow on each end. His teacher marks the line wrong. Why?
options: Because a relation with a negative slope has to be shown with a dashed line
Because the arrows go the wrong way, so the line must stop at the last dot
Because only those 5 integer x-values exist, so the dots stay separate
Because only the dots in Quadrant II and Quadrant IV may be joined up
questions.explain: The table gives only 5 integer inputs, so there is no point at x = 1.5 and the graph is 5 separate dots. A line or arrows would wrongly claim that every value in between belongs to the relation.

questions.question: Jaya builds a table of values for y = -2x + 3 using x = -4, -2, 0, 2, 4. For x = -4 she correctly gets y = 11, but then she plots that dot 4 units right of the origin and 11 units down. Which correction is right?
options: The dot is right, since a negative x always goes with down
The dot belongs 4 right and 11 up, since y = 11 is positive
The dot belongs 4 left and 11 down, which is Quadrant III
The dot belongs 4 left and 11 up, which is Quadrant II
questions.explain: The x-coordinate -4 controls only the left-right move and y = 11 controls the up-down move, so the dot is 4 left and 11 up, in Quadrant II. A negative x means left; it does not turn y negative as well.
